<system-reminder>
Instruction files were re-read when this session started; these differ from their earlier copies — each replaces its earlier copy, and the instructions preamble above still applies:

Contents of /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1/AGENTS.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

# AGENTS.md - Agent Instructions

The universal core of the agent instructions: the dual-repo model, the hard rules, the cycle
protocol, and a map of the rest. One of the [agent-files](#terminology), carried by every adopter.
The rules are an index: each is a sentence and a link to the section that holds it, and a
section's why is in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md) under the mirrored heading.

## Terminology

Repos: the two repos of [the dual-repo model](#the-dual-repo-model), "work-repo" and "agent-repo",
always hyphenated.

Agent-files: the instruction set an agent reads, `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*`. `TODO.md` is not
one, since its content is the project's record, but the agent-files require that there is one, of
the shape in [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format), and a `zTOC.md` beside it holding the
cycle's ladder and the files worth knowing ([zTOC format](agent-data/notes.md#ztoc-format)).

Agent-files version: the set's own version, `vX.Y.Z`, the name of an empty
`agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z` file, bumped by `agent-files` proposal cycles and copied by
adoptions ([Agent-files version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).

Set: the agent-files as an adopter carries them, the copy a new repo starts from, applied by
`scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` from that adopter's working copy, or with `--landed` from its trunk.
Adopter: a project carrying a copy of the set.
Proposer: the adopter a proposal comes from. There is no maintainer and no template repository, only
adopters and proposers, and the copy a proposal starts from is whichever adopter's the proposer
took.

Cycle: one change, run from opening to closing as one commit or a ladder of them, each made by
`vc-x1 commit` ([Cycle protocol](#cycle-protocol)). Its shape is its branch's commit count, a
single-step cycle being one commit above the trunk and a multi-step one more ([Cycle
shape](#cycle-shape)). Both run on a bookmark, and both stay on this machine until the Land unless
the user decides otherwise.

Land: the sequence that makes a cycle permanent, on the user's go at the close-out: sync, integrate,
publish, install ([Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)). `vc-x1 land` names its
integrate step alone, and a rule writes "Land" for the sequence and `vc-x1 land` for the command.
Land is onto the trunk, `[cycle] trunk`, `main` when absent. Before it the cycle is a draft on its
bookmark, after it the commits are permanent.

Trapezoid: the default close-out shape, a merge commit whose first parent is the trunk line and
whose second is the cycle's ladder ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)). Names
both the merge commit and the figure the graph draws around it.

Artifact: the work-repo's built product. A cycle runs its own dev build, installed beside the plain
name ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)), and the plain name is
installed at Land.

Rationale: a rule's why, in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md) under the heading that mirrors
the rule's, reached by `[why](agent-data/rationale.md#<same-slug>)`. Read when changing a rule,
not when following one.

## The dual-repo model

Two separate jj-git colocated repos ([jj.md](agent-data/jj.md)), located by a `.vc-config.md`,
never by the current directory ([.vc-config.md](agent-data/jj.md#vc-configmd),
[why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-dual-repo-model)):

1. Work-repo: the project's work product. Its directory is the workspace root, the directory
   holding the work-repo's `.vc-config.md`, whose `[repos] work` is `"."`.
2. Agent-repo: the agent's session data, in the directory that file's `[repos] agent` names, a
   path relative to the workspace root or an absolute one, so it may sit anywhere. Written
   `<agent-dir>` wherever a command below needs it, and reached by Claude Code through a symlink
   at `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-project-path>`, which `vc-x1 init` creates for a dual
   workspace and `vc-x1 symlink` creates on demand.

## Rules

The rules, indexed: each a one-sentence summary and a link to the section that states it, this
file's rules first and then the outer files' in their order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#rules)).
The section is the rule, the sentence its handle. None is absolute: a rule bends only when the
user says so explicitly, at the moment or as a scoped delegation ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask) is
the path), and the exception is recorded in the cycle's records, naming what the bend covers and
what it does not, so a waiver over a cycle's pushes says whether Land is inside it. No rule bends
silently.

- Read custom.md first: when a `custom.md` exists, the agent must read it first, it overrides
  anything in the agent-files, and it holds what is local to the workspace
  ([custom.md](#custommd)).
- Acquaint before work: a session acquaints first, and what its repo check finds is reported and
  left as found until the user says how to proceed ([Acquaint](#acquaint)).
- Sync where `main` matters: a look at acquaint and a sync at the opening, the closing, and Land,
  each reported, and a repo held back stops the step ([Sync](#sync)).
- A session's rules are its own agent-files: the ones it started in, binding in every repo it
  writes, and another repo's rules bind only by delegation ([A session's rules are its own
  agent-files](#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)).
- Bookmark per cycle: a cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, and `main` advances
  only when the cycle lands ([Cycles run on a bookmark](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)).
- Shape by count: a branch with one commit above the trunk is single-step and more is a ladder, and
  a ladder lands as a trapezoid, never squashed ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)).
- Local by default: a cycle's commits stay on this machine until the Land, and the user decides when
  each side commits and publishes ([A cycle is local by default](#a-cycle-is-local-by-default)).
- Read the step before the action: [The per-rung flow](#the-per-rung-flow) before commit work,
  [Before any push](#before-any-push) before a push, from the file, not from memory.
- Commit by the tool: a cycle rung is committed only by `vc-x1 commit` ([Committing vs
  pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)).
- Approval per push: only a push publishes, and every push needs the user's explicit approval, or an
  explicit waiver ([Before any push](#before-any-push)).
- Hard stop after the final push: after the turn's final push nothing until the user speaks,
  unless an explicit waiver ([At rest](#at-rest)).
- One command per invocation: no bundled steps, except a genuine pipeline or a tight pair
  ([Working practices](#working-practices)).
- Exit status: the command under test runs bare and last, `set -o pipefail` first when piped, and
  `bash-guard.sh` denies the masks it can see ([Working practices](#working-practices)).
- Stop and ask: on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes
  on a simple task has produced no progress ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask)).
- Changing the agent-files: a change to the rules is tried in the local copy, then proposed as one
  set of diffs, which an adopter accepts as is, negotiates, or declines ([Changing the
  agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)).
- jj, not git: version-control operations use jj ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
- No hand-written trailers: `vc-x1 commit` stamps the trailers, never write one by hand
  ([ochid trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).
- No re-describe without coordinating: never `jj describe` a published or trailer-carrying
  commit ([Re-describing](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)).
- Prose style: durable text is in the prose form, typeable punctuation included ([Prose
  form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form)).
- One title per step: the ladder rung and the commit title are verbatim identical
  ([Conventional-commit shape](agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit)).
- Alert on unwrap: say so when introducing an `unwrap` / `expect` / `unwrap_or*` site, with its
  `// OK: ...` comment ([`// OK` comments](agent-data/code.md#-ok--comments-on-unwrap-calls-rust)).

## Acquaint

What a session does first, at its start and whenever the user says "acquaint" or "reacquaint",
in this order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#acquaint)):

1. custom.md: when there is one, read it, and do what it asks for at acquaint
   ([custom.md](#custommd)).
2. Hooks: `bash agent-data/hooks.sh check`, and what it finds missing, different, or
   unregistered is reported for the user to install ([Working practices](#working-practices)).
3. Tools: `vc-x1 -V` and `vc-x1-dev -V`, both reported, and a dev build newer than the plain one
   is the user's to choose ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)).
4. Repo check: look at each repo of the workspace for the four findings below, and report what is
   found before anything else. Nothing is opened, pushed, rebased, committed, or discarded until
   the user says how to proceed.
   - Not up to date: a repo whose `main` is behind, ahead of, or diverged from its remote's, as
     the look reports it ([Sync](#sync)), run again with `--bookmark <bookmark>` when a cycle is
     in flight. A look that fails is reported as the check not made.
   - Uncommitted work: a work-repo `@` that is not empty, as `jj st` prints it. What the
     continuation notes account for, the notes themselves or a rung in flight they describe, is
     theirs to direct at step 5, and any other change is a finding. The agent-repo's `@` holds the
     session's own data and is never one.
   - Work off `main`: commits on a bookmark, a cycle's or any other, that do not descend from the
     remote's `main`. The user is told, and a rebase onto `main` is suggested.
   - Conflicts: a conflicted commit or working copy, as `jj st` and `jj log -r 'conflicts()'` show
     them. The acquaint stops there and the user is informed.
5. TODO.md: read the acquaint slice ([File
   reads](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)), the continuation notes first,
   each acted on, filed or kept, and the section reset ([Todo
   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
6. Report: say where things stand, the cycle in flight, its ladder in `zTOC.md`, or the top of `##
   Todo`, and wait.

## Sync

One command, `vc-x1 sync -s b`, brings both repos up to date, each `main` at the commit
its remote's `main` is at. It runs at the moments a cycle depends on `main`, and what it prints
is reported ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#sync)):

- Acquaint looks: with `--dry-run`, which moves nothing, so each repo is reported as found.
- Opening syncs: as its first step, which is its rung's step 0, so the cycle's bookmark is
  created on an up-to-date `main`.
- Closing syncs: at its rung's step 0, so the record and version it carries are made from an
  up-to-date `main`. A rung between may sync at its step 0, the agent's or the user's call.
- Land syncs: as its first step, and a `main` the sync moved stops the Land.

A sync that fails or holds a repo back stops the step until the user says how to proceed, as does
one at a rung's step 0 that moved a `main`, and `--force` and `--rebase` are the user's to ask
for.

## Cycle protocol

How a [cycle](#terminology) runs ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-protocol)). Its record is
`TODO.md > ## In Progress` and nothing else ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)). The `.vc-config.md`
`[validate]` table defines the commands that validate the work-repo.

### Cycles run on a bookmark

A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, created at the opening and named by the cycle
title's slug ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). `main` advances only when
the finished cycle lands on it, so development is never done on `main`, a single-step cycle
included. The agent-repo needs no bookmark. Commands in [Cycle
bookmarks](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), the long-lived case in [Long-lived
bookmarks][llb].

### Cycle shape

A cycle's shape is its branch's commit count, so nothing has to be decided before its first commit
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-shape)).

- Every cycle starts with `vc-x1 commit --opening`, a single-step cycle included: it creates the
  bookmark at the trunk, and its one commit begins as the opening.
- One commit above the trunk is single-step: `vc-x1 commit --closing <BM|REV>` finalizes that commit
  in place, the bare cycle title replacing the opening's, and it carries the opening's duties, the
  work, and the close-out's duties.
- More commits are a ladder: `--closing` makes the closing commit, the merge of the trunk and the
  ladder's tip. Every closing names its tip, by the cycle's bookmark or a revision, `@-` the common
  one, so there is no bare form. A tip that is not `@-` is closed by a detour, `@` moving onto it
  and returning after, and the commits above it stay as they are.
- A ladder lands as a trapezoid, never squashed: every rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, and a
  squash discards all but one. We think a linear closing, a plain commit on the ladder, follows as
  a `--shape` flag, which is proposed and not built.
- The closing's title and body may be left out: the cycle title is read from the opening, and the
  body comes from `.vc-config.md`'s `[closing] body`.
- A dead end still closes and lands: a cycle abandoned after its opening keeps what is worth
  keeping, reverts the rest, and records what was tried, why it stopped, and what replaces it. Its
  closing is `--closing <BM|REV> --dead-end`, titled with the cycle title plus " dead-end closing".

### Unplanned work

Work that arrives while a cycle runs goes one of two ways, and the user picks which
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#unplanned-work)):

- A rung inserted into the ladder, usually when it is inside the cycle's subject or blocks it.
- A `## Todo` or `## Waiting` entry, run as its own cycle later.

A rung inserted while the working copy already holds the next rung's edits sets those edits aside
first, as a jj commit with a local bookmark, never a patch file, so the inserted rung's commit
carries its own change alone, and they return once it is made.

### Cycle-record

A cycle's record is its `TODO.md > ## In Progress` block and nothing else, the cycle-record
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-record)).

- Items: title, problem, solution, acceptance check, deliberation, and the rung subsections, the
  ladder over them being `zTOC.md`'s, all provisional until close-out ([The In Progress
  block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)).
- Life: written at the opening, revised as rungs land, finalized by the closing commit, which moves
  it whole to `## Closed` (a single-step cycle's one commit writes it there directly), deleted by
  the next opening.
  - `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles.
  - Its ladder, each rung with its marker, is `zTOC.md`'s, kept by the closing so the landmark holds
    it and replaced by the next opening ([zTOC format](agent-data/notes.md#ztoc-format)).
  - The closing commit's tree carries the final form, and the file never grows.
- After that jj holds it: `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds the commits, on the title the
  pushed bookends carry when a rename came mid-cycle, and the landmark on `main` (the trapezoid
  merge, or the single-step commit) holds the finished block in its `TODO.md > ## Closed`.
- No backfill: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
- Never amended: a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it is found, citing the
  landmark.
- May be reworked while local: while a cycle's work commits are local and its agent `@` uncommitted,
  an earlier commit's record may be reworked. By default it is unnecessary, a later rung revising
  the record, and it is permitted when the error is significant, a word left to whoever is reading.
  A reworked commit's tree is validated again.
- Design findings that must outlive the cycle go into a `notes/` file by the rung that made them,
  never left in the block.
- Frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` are never appended, still linked.

### Opening

The cycle's first commit, which needs no setup of its own when the cycle is small, and it then
carries steps 1 and 2. A single-step cycle does all of it in its one commit, after steps 1 and 2
([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)). Before that commit ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#opening)):

1. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), whatever the cycle's form.
2. Bookmark: `vc-x1 commit --opening` creates it, kept local, so there is nothing to do before the
   commit but name it.
3. Waiting: check each `## Waiting` entry's condition, and promote what is met into `## Todo` at
   the rank it names.
4. In Progress block: delete whatever `## Closed` holds, then move the chosen `## Todo` entry into
   `## In Progress`, shaped as [The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)
   says, the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and write its ladder into
   `zTOC.md > ## Ladder` in place of the last cycle's.
5. Bump: bump the version-of-record to the opening's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), and the agent-files version with it when the
   cycle is an `agent-files` proposal ([Agent-files
   version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).

Rungs are named, not numbered ([Steps are named, not numbered][snn]), and a multi-step cycle's
bookends are the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing" ([Cycle bookend titles][cbt]).

### The per-rung flow

Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)):

0. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), required at the opening and the closing, optional
   between, the agent's or the user's call.
1. Mark current: mark the rung `(current)` in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`, as the first edit, with the
   version suffix step 2 gives it.
2. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), the agent-files version beside it in an
   `agent-files` proposal cycle.
3. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
4. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under `####
   Rungs`. The rung stays `(current)` until step 7.
5. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites
   files (`cargo fmt`), so use `--fast` while a review iterates. A failure is read and its cause
   named before validation runs again, and a failure that does not repeat is a finding, reported
   and given a Todo entry. A rung that changes the artifact then installs the working copy's dev
   build, `vc-x1 install --profile dev`, so the review runs the code under review, and again after
   each review fix ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)).
6. Work review: stop before writing any description and say "please review", as its own message with
   no title or body. Iterate until the user says "continue" / "go". The review is of the
   working-copy diff ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
7. Flip and describe: flip `(current)` to `(done)` the moment "done" is true, then write the
   description in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), read from the file first
   with its specimen, [commit-model.md](agent-data/commit-model.md) ([Commit
   description](#commit-description)). A local description can still be changed before the Land, so
   it has no review of its own.
8. Commit: on the go, `vc-x1 commit -s w --title "..." --body "..."`, local ([Committing vs
   pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)), `--opening` added for the opening and `--closing <BM|REV>`
   for the closing ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)). A rung that changes the artifact then installs its
   dev build again, so the next rung runs the committed code, not the working copy's ([Dev artifact
   name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)).

### Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 commit`, never by `jj commit`, and published only by `vc-x1
push` ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#committing-vs-pushing)).

- `vc-x1 commit` stays on this machine and needs no approval, and `--local` says so outright. So
  does `vc-x1 land`.
- `vc-x1 push`, exactly like `commit --push` or `land --push`, publishes, as does `squash-push`.
- `vc-x1 squash` continues a rung, folding the working copy into it. `squash --title --body` is the
  sanctioned re-describe of `@-`, and `commit -r REV --title --body` describes a commit made by
  hand.
- A bare `jj commit` is asked for by name and is for local saves and [local ladder](#local-ladders)
  intermediates. What the commands do is in [vc-x1 commit and push][vpush].

#### A cycle is local by default

A cycle's commits stay on this machine until its Land, and the user decides when each side is
committed and when either is published, at any rung, every push still taking its own approval
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#a-cycle-is-local-by-default)).

- The default: every commit is `vc-x1 commit -s w`, the opening's bookmark created and not pushed,
  and the agent `@` holds the session until an agent commit is made.
- Any mix of work and agent commits is valid. `commit -s b` makes a 1:1 pair, `commit -s w` rungs
  then `commit -s a --covers <REVSET>` or the Land make N:1, and several agent commits naming one
  work commit make 1:M. The rule is the links: a work commit's `ochid:` names each agent change it
  pairs with, an agent commit's names each work commit it covers, each below an `orepo:` naming the
  other repo, and a squash folds into a commit an `ochid:` names, never that commit away, since jj
  keeps the change id of the commit squashed into ([Cross-repo
  linking](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).
- A backup, a move between machines, or someone else to see the cycle commits the agent side and
  publishes mid-cycle: `commit -s a --covers <REVSET>`, then `push -s b`.
- The Land commits the agent `@` first, one `ochid:` per work commit it has not yet covered, an
  older work commit's `ocid:` and `pcid:` giving way to `orepo:`, trees unchanged.
- We think a cycle's whole transcript in one commit may near jj's new-file size limit, and the
  mid-cycle backup's two commands want one.

### Commit description

The title is a Conventional Commit, distinct within its cycle ([Commit titles and
descriptions][cdd]).
The body is in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), two plain paragraphs: no
version, file list, or deliberation ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#commit-description)).

### Pushing

Pushing is by `vc-x1 push`, and the Land's bookmark moves are `vc-x1 land` and `delete-bookmark`.

#### Before any push

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#before-any-push))

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver covers it. `vc-x1 push
  --yes` is for that approval alone, since an agent can type it as easily as anything else.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are written. Nothing follows the turn's final push.

#### At rest

The contract that keeps the work-repo clean, the rule **Hard stop after the final push** its first
item's tail ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#at-rest)):

1. The agent publishes: a step that publishes is complete when its command is issued. The agent says
   what is worth saying *before* the final publishing command, responds with the one word
   "Published", and does nothing further until the user speaks.
2. Clean by squash-push: a Land is published by the agent only with the user's permission. A run of
   delegated cycles follows each `land --push` with the next `commit --opening`, which carries the
   session's tail. A Land the agent made locally is published by the user after the session:
   `vc-x1 squash-push -s b` pushes the work trunk and folds the tail into the Land's agent commit
   and pushes it, so each `main` moves once, forward, the two in either order, since no trailer
   holds a SHA.
   `squash-push` refuses a push that would be forced, a published commit rewritten, without
   `--force`.

"Clean" means the work `@` is empty, and once the user's squash-push has run the agent's `@` too.
Before it the agent's `@` is the session's data and no finding, as [Acquaint](#acquaint) says. A
late work-repo tweak after a push is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push ([vc-x1
commit and push][vpush]).

### Close-out

The cycle's last commit is bookkeeping and its body describes that bookkeeping. A single-step cycle
does all of it in its one commit, step 5 aside ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)):

1. Acceptance check: run the check the opening stated and record pass or fail. A rung may run it and
   the closing record the result, since some checks run only mid-ladder. A failure is a finding, and
   why it failed is determined.
2. Finalize the cycle-record in place ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)):
   - sync the title if the scope shifted, and every anchor back-reference with it. A published rung
     title and the bookend pair keep their names, so a rename then reaches the block's text and the
     rungs not yet published only
   - replace the provisional solution statement with what was done
   - add the design subsections the deliberation grew
   - complete the closing rung's subsection
   - ask what in the block must outlive the cycle, and write it into the `notes/` file it
     belongs to
   - move the block whole to `## Closed`, leaving `## In Progress` reading
     `_No cycle currently in progress._`, which `vc-x1 commit --closing` does, and `zTOC.md`'s
     ladder as it is, with every marker final.
3. Validate: full validation, and update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
4. Size: when an agent-file changed, record the line count in `notes/agent-files-size.md`,
   smaller being the quasi-goal. A cycle that touched none adds no row.
5. Close-out shape ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)): a ladder closes as a
   trapezoid, the closing commit carrying the shape, so nothing is reshaped at Land.
6. Continuation notes: anything the next agent needs is written into `TODO.md > ## Continuation
   notes`, the first section, before the closing commit, which carries them, so the work-repo is
   clean from the Land on. A fact known only after the Land is not written: the note names what the
   next session checks, `main` at the closing, the bookmarks gone, the installed version's commit.
   The next acquaint reads it first, files or keeps each item, and resets the section ([Todo
   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
7. Land: on the user's go, the sequence in [Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).
8. Restart: the user restarts the agent.

### Local ladders

A rung that wants incremental review runs as a local ladder: a chain of jj commits that never leaves
the machine and collapses into the rung before the cycle continues, each validated with
`vc-x1 validate --fast` ([Local ladders](agent-data/jj.md#local-ladders),
[why](agent-data/rationale.md#local-ladders)).

## Working practices

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#working-practices))

- One command per invocation: no bundled steps (`a && b; c`), except a genuine pipeline or a tight
  pair where the join is the point.
- Exit status: never mask a command's exit status. The command under test runs bare and last in
  its invocation, since the Bash tool reports a nonzero exit, with `set -o pipefail` first when it
  is piped. No `&&` after a piped stage, no trailing `; echo "exit=$?"`. To report and still fail:
  `cmd || { rc=$?; echo failed=$rc; exit $rc; }`.
- Hooks: the Claude Code hooks are in `agent-data/` and `bash agent-data/hooks.sh install`, the
  user's to run, puts them in `~/.claude/hooks/` and registers them in `~/.claude/settings.json`.
  `bash-guard.sh` denies the two masks it can see, an echo of `$?` or `PIPESTATUS` and a `cargo`
  or `vc-x1` command piped into `tail`, `head`, `grep`, or `rg` without `pipefail`. `bash-allow.sh`
  skips the prompt for `cargo`, `jj`, and `vc-x1`, and `inhibit-sleep.sh` keeps the machine awake
  while a session works.
- Scratch files: where a thing goes is decided by whether it can be reproduced.
  - `tmp/`: disposable, cleared at any time, gitignored, `mkdir -p tmp` on demand. `/tmp` is for
    out-of-project temporaries.
  - `tmp-durable/`, gitignored beside it: what we would rather not lose and can reproduce, a built
    index for one.
  - `notes/`: what must last, committed and pushed. It holds no pointer into `tmp-durable/`.
  - Code set aside: a jj commit with a local bookmark, not pushed, so either of us can address it,
    never a patch file.
- Slice reads: read the slice you need from long notes files. The acquaint read is `TODO.md`
  `offset=0, limit=60` ([notes.md](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).
- https remotes: use https remotes, and check for an ssh remote first when a push dies at the
  network leg. A remote URL change needs the user's go.
- Delegate: mechanical subtasks go to lesser models (Opus/Haiku/Sonnet).
- No memory directory: `~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/` is unused, the agent-files are.
- Speculation: mark it in durable text with "We think ..." ([Speculation
  marker](agent-data/prose.md#speculation-marker)).
- Plain synopsis: end a technical explanation in conversation with one, marked "The plain version:"
  ([Plain synopsis](agent-data/prose.md#plain-synopsis-after-technical-explanations)).

### A session's rules are its own agent-files

A session's rules are the agent-files of the project it started in, and its `custom.md`, and rules
living in any other repo are ignored unless these files or the user direct otherwise
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)). So another repo's own
protocol (a shared store's README, another project's agent-files) governs a write to it only as
far as the delegation reaches, and this file's conduct rules, the step reads, the reviews, the
per-push approval, and the stops, bind every commit and push the session makes, in any repo,
cycle or not. A repo with a live agent of its own is not written at all: message its agent.

### Stop and ask

Stop and ask on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes on a
simple task has produced no progress ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#stop-and-ask)).

## Changing the agent-files

A new repo starts from an adopter's set, its working copy's by default, applied by
`scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh`, and every adopter carries its own copy
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

- Local experiments: a local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment, diffed against the copy it
  started from while the rules are being tried. After the experiment there may be a proposal.
- Proposing: a proposal is one set of diffs, to the rules or beyond them, that an adopter may or
  may not accept as is.
- Convergence: the adopter reviews the diff between the proposal and its files and accepts it as is
  or proposes changes. It is a negotiation whose goal is everyone accepting the same thing, and
  that goal is not a requirement.
- Acceptance: the adopter and the proposer agree on the contents, identical or not.
- Retirement: a resolved experiment retires like a finished Todo, adopted and rejected alike: the
  cycle that resolved it is its record.

## custom.md

When a `custom.md` exists at the workspace root, the agent must read it first, and it overrides
anything in the agent-files ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#custommd)). It is the place for what is
local to the workspace, one machine's paths and permissions, since a change every clone needs is a
cycle on the agent-file it belongs in. The session lock,
[session-lock.md](agent-data/session-lock.md), is an experiment it may carry.

content.text:
Yes, I think we should say it. I'd call it the preferred order rather than a must:

- **Correctness doesn't depend on it.** The links are change ids, so they hold whichever repo is pushed first.
- **Your reason is about failure.** The work-repo is the shared one, so its push is the one likely to be refused, because someone else pushed to it first. If it goes first and is refused, nothing has been published and the agent side is still only on this machine. The agent-repo usually has one user, so its push rarely fails.
- **Agent first is the worse failure.** If the work push is then refused, the agent `main` is already public and names a work commit nobody else can see. You'd fix the work side, rebasing and maybe restamping, while the agent side is already out.

Now that every command pushes work first, the rule can stop saying "either order" and give the reason. I'd put it in four places:

- **`AGENTS.md` At rest, item 2:** "…`vc-x1 squash-push -s b` pushes the work trunk first, the shared repo and so the push likely to be refused, then folds the tail into the Land's agent commit and pushes it, so each `main` moves once, forward."
- **`jj.md` Land, step 3:** "the work repo first" in place of "the two repos in either order".
- **`rationale.md`, the paragraph the test added:** keep "either order is correct, since no trailer holds a SHA". Add: "Work first is preferred (wink, 2026-11-09): the work-repo is the shared one, so its push is the one a concurrent push refuses, and refused first it leaves nothing published."
- **The comment in `push_in`** gets the same reason in a line.

`squash-push -s b`, `push -s b` and `land --push` already do this, so it's wording only. Shall I make the edits?

The plain version: either order keeps the links correct, but the shared work-repo is the push most likely to fail, so pushing it first means a failure leaves nothing half-published. Worth saying in the rule and the rationale.

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

Solution: a loader finds and reads the file and a parser takes text and
returns the schema, so a test hands the parser a string, and `main` gets
the schema from one call. See details in TODO.md.
```

The first paragraph states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes.
The second opens "Solution:" and ends with the pointer, and nothing names a file that the diff
already lists.

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". See details in

```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body names the cycle by its title and points at

I agree, with two changes. Rung -1's trailers have to be fixed first, and I'd push both repos, not just the agent repo.

**Rung -1 still has the old trailers.** `tlsszorkmswv` was committed by 0.85.21-1, before the orepo code, and carries:

```
ochid: msxzosrsqltq
ocid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1.agent-session/commit/xxxx
pcid: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/c39b56d7…
```

That `ocid:` still has its `xxxx` placeholder. Once published, -1 can't be changed without a forced push, so it would stay malformed for good. It's local now, so `trailers --update` (rung 1's own feature) can restamp it to `orepo:` plus `ochid:`.

The range has to be given explicitly. The default, from the trunk up to `@-`, includes the opening, which is already on origin under the topic bookmark. Restamping the opening would mean a forced push. The opening keeps its `ocid:`/`pcid:` lines, which validate-desc now ignores.

**The agent commit.** Both rungs already name the agent `@`, `msxzosrsqltq`. So `commit -s a --covers` makes exactly the commit you describe: one agent commit with `orepo:` naming vc-x1, then one `ochid:` per rung, oldest first. It's the mid-cycle backup in the rules. At the Land, the next agent commit covers the rungs that follow.

**Push both, work first.** If only the agent repo goes out, its `ochid:` lines name work commits nobody else can see, which is what the rule we just wrote avoids. `push -s b` fast-forwards the cycle bookmark, already on origin from the opening, to -2, then folds the journal into `msxzosrsqltq` and pushes agent `main`. It's still a WIP bookmark, and `main` doesn't move.

The sequence:

1. `vc-x1-dev trailers --update --range 'tlsszorkmswv::pmtvruwwsrvo' --dry-run`, then the same command without `--dry-run`. This is local, and only -1 should change, since -2 is already in the new form.
2. `vc-x1-dev commit -s a --covers 'tlsszorkmswv::pmtvruwwsrvo' --dry-run`, then for real. This is local too, and I'd title it "chore: the session through feat: orepo replaces ocid and pcid".
3. `vc-x1-dev push -s b`, the push, which needs your approval.

The plain version: rung -1 still carries a placeholder trailer and has to be restamped before it's published. Then one agent commit can name both rungs, and `push -s b` publishes the work rungs and that agent commit together, work first. Say go and I'll run steps 1 and 2 and stop before the push.

content.text:
I agree. With no SHA in any trailer, nothing requires the agent repo to stay unchanged until the Land, and that was the only reason to hold the agent side back as one commit per cycle. Making a pair at every rung (`commit -s b`) is now the simpler default.

**Why each rung should get its own agent commit:**
- **The record:** each rung's agent commit holds the conversation up to that rung. You can see the discussion behind a change without searching one cycle-sized commit.
- **The links:** one `ochid:` each way per rung. N:1 agent commits stay possible but are no longer the normal case.
- **The size concern goes away:** the rules say "We think a cycle's whole transcript in one commit may near jj's new-file size limit". With pairs, the transcript file is tracked at the first rung, so it's never a large new file again.
- **Clean-up stays the same:** after a session, `squash-push -s b` folds the tail into the last rung's agent commit, which is still unpublished.

**What it doesn't change:** committing in pairs isn't pushing in pairs. Each rung is still committed only on this machine, and every push still needs your approval. Pairs make it possible to publish rung by rung, but don't require it.

**Rungs -1 and -2 can't honestly be made into pairs.** Both already name the same agent `@`, and the transcript can't be split back at the moment -1 was committed. A second agent commit for -2 would be made up. So I'd keep the plan from before for these two:
1. Restamp -1.
2. Make one agent commit covering both.
3. `push -s b`.

**From rung 3 on, the rules change:**
- **Per-rung flow, step 8:** `vc-x1 commit -s b` in place of `-s w`.
- **"A cycle is local by default":** its default bullet becomes "every commit is `commit -s b`", still not pushed. The Land's agent commit then only covers what's left over.
- **rationale.md:** an entry giving the reason, that holding the agent side back only protected `ocid:`'s SHA.
- **The size-limit note** comes out.

That's a rule change, so I'd add it to the ladder as its own rung before "chore: a test vc-x2 reaches vc-x1's history", maybe "feat: a rung commits as a pair". Its own commit would be the first made with `-s b`.

The plain version: the agent side was held back only to keep a SHA stable, and that's gone, so each rung can commit with its own agent partner. Pushing stays your call per push. The two rungs already made can't be split honestly, so they get one shared agent commit. Say go and I'll do the restamp and that agent commit, stop before the push, then add the new rung.

content.text:
You're right that the guard isn't gated on the Land. I built it to refuse any forced push, and that's broader than what you described. With agent repos treated as personal but public, I think the agent side shouldn't be refused at all.

**What you asked for vs what's built.**
- **Your concern:** a delegated run. I publish a Land, the next `commit --opening` carries the tail, and you then do a squash-push.
- **What's built:** a refusal in every repo, for any fold into a published commit or any push where origin isn't below the target. So it also blocks your old habit of folding a session's tail into the last agent commit, which has nothing to do with a Land.

**Why the agent side can drop the guard.**
- **No link breaks:** a forced update of agent `main` replaces SHAs, and the links are change ids.
- **No one is affected:** if agent repos aren't usually cloned, nobody holds the old commit, so nothing diverges for anyone.
- **The history stays visible:** someone reading the history on GitHub sees the agent commit with its tail. That's what a clean agent repo means.
- **The delegated case is harmless:** a fold after a published Land just moves the tail into the Land's agent commit. That's tidy, if unnecessary, since the next opening would carry it.

**Why the work side keeps it.** The work trunk is shared and cloned, and forcing it hurts others. That's the case the refusal is for.

**So the proposal:**
- **Agent repo:** `squash-push` force-updates without asking. A report line says so, something like "'main' is published, so its push is forced, the agent repo being personal".
- **Work repo:** keeps the refusal, with `--force` as the opt-in.
- **Gating on the Land itself** (refuse only when the agent commit covers a published Land) is possible, but it adds machinery for a case the personal assumption already covers. I'd leave it for vc-x2's look at agent repos.

**When to make it.** This rung introduced the guard and isn't pushed yet, so I'd fold the change into it as a review fix (`vc-x1 squash` into `pmtvruwwsrvo`), then push. Otherwise -2 goes public with a guard we already know is wrong for the agent repo.

For vc-x2's Todo I'd record the assumption itself: agent repos are personal but public, observed rather than cloned, with forced updates as its consequence.

The plain version: the guard stops your old agent clean-up habit, and it shouldn't, because nobody else holds the agent repo and no link depends on its SHAs. I'd keep it for the shared work repo only, fix it in rung -2 before we push, and leave the deeper question to vc-x2.

1	//! The `squash-push` subcommand: squash the working copy into its
2	//! parent, advance a bookmark, and push: capture a repo's trailing
3	//! writes and publish them in one step.
4	//!
5	//! - Built for the agent repo, whose working copy accumulates session
6	//!   data continuously (the session tail): after a session it folds
7	//!   the tail into the last agent commit and publishes it, so both
8	//!   repos are clean. The change id of the commit folded into is kept,
9	//!   so the `ochid:` naming it still resolves.
10	//! - Refuses a push that would be forced, its target already on the
11	//!   bookmark's remote or the remote not below it, before changing
12	//!   anything, so a published trunk is never rewritten. `--force`
13	//!   allows it, for a work-in-progress bookmark: an amend-and-push.
14	//! - Runs synchronously: preflight validations, then squash +
15	//!   bookmark-set + push. A failure is a visible non-zero exit
16	//!   (the retired 0.69.0-2 predecessor delegated to a detached
17	//!   child that a sandboxed run silently killed: the loss
18	//!   diagnosed in 0.68.1).
19	//! - Prechecks and after-checks with one verdict: the working copy
20	//!   and the bookmark's publish state from `status`, plus this
21	//!   command's own question of whether the bookmark has reached the
22	//!   squash target. A run with nothing to do prints `<label>: clean`
23	//!   and stops, and every other run prints the line again after the
24	//!   push. The after-check reports only, since the exit code is the
25	//!   push's.
26	//! - Asks before acting, when asking is on. `squash-push.yes` sets
27	//!   the default and is true, so today's behavior is what a bare run
28	//!   gets, `--ask` turns the prompt on, and `--yes` turns it off,
29	//!   since a boolean flag cannot turn a configured true back off.
30	//!   With the prompt on, a non-tty stdin is an error rather than a
31	//!   hang, and a declined prompt is an error too.
32	//! - Reports an at-rest publish mismatch (BOOKMARK not matching
33	//!   `BOOKMARK@origin`, an earlier publish was lost) and proceeds:
34	//!   publishing is the command's job, so healing is not
35	//!   auto-fixing.
36	//! - Says nothing and asks nothing as push's `squash-push-bot`
37	//!   stage, which `at_rest` marks. Every line above is addressed to
38	//!   a person, and mid-push there is neither a person to read them
39	//!   nor a state worth describing. The precheck's decision still
40	//!   applies, so a stage with nothing to do still does nothing.
41	
42	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
43	
44	use clap::Args;
45	use log::{debug, info, warn};
46	
47	use crate::context::Context;
48	use crate::desc_helpers::extract_ochids;
49	use crate::jj;
50	use crate::options_flags::scope::{
51	    ALL_REPO_SCOPES, REPO_SCOPE_FORMS, RepoScope, repo_scope_parser,
52	};
53	use crate::options_flags::squash::{SquashOption, SquashSpec};
54	use crate::status;
55	use crate::subcommand::SubcommandRunner;
56	
57	/// Squash `@` into `@-`, advance BOOKMARK, and push, in each
58	/// scoped repo.
59	///
60	/// Captures a repo's trailing working-copy writes into the last
61	/// commit and publishes it. A push that would be forced, an
62	/// already-pushed commit rewritten, is refused without `--force`.
63	/// `-s` is required: `squash-push -s a` is the
64	/// agent repo's session tail folded and pushed, `-s w` or `-s b`
65	/// the fold-and-publish that asks nothing, and `-s p` a plain repo.
66	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
67	pub struct SquashPushArgs {
68	    /// Retired: the bookmark, now `--bookmark`, refused naming it.
69	    #[arg(value_name = "RETIRED", hide = true)]
70	    pub retired: Option<String>,
71	
72	    /// Bookmark to advance and push [default: the bookmark of the
73	    /// line you are on, the nearest one at or above the squash
74	    /// target]
75	    #[arg(long, value_name = "NAME")]
76	    pub bookmark: Option<String>,
77	
78	    /// Where: a path in the workspace for `-s w|a|b`, its root or
79	    /// either repo, or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the
80	    /// current directory]
81	    #[arg(short = 'R', long, value_name = "PATH")]
82	    pub repo: Option<PathBuf>,

85	    #[arg(
86	        short = 's',
87	        long,
88	        value_name = "SCOPE",
89	        value_parser = repo_scope_parser(ALL_REPO_SCOPES),
90	        required = true,
91	        help = format!("Which repo(s), required: {REPO_SCOPE_FORMS}")
92	    )]
93	    pub scope: RepoScope,
94	
95	    #[command(flatten)]
96	    pub squash: SquashOption,
97

99	    #[arg(short = 'y', long = "yes", conflicts_with = "ask")]
100	    pub yes: bool,
101	
102	    /// Ask before acting, overriding a configured squash-push.yes
103	    #[arg(long = "ask")]
104	    pub ask: bool,
105	
106	    /// Push even when the push is forced, a commit already published
107	    /// rewritten, which is refused without it: for a work-in-progress
108	    /// bookmark, never a trunk
109	    #[arg(long)]
110	    pub force: bool,
111

113	    /// change nothing

118	/// Per-invocation squash-push inputs: the clap-free shape the op
119	/// works against. Built from `SquashPushArgs` at the binary edge
120	/// via `TryFrom` (fallible only on repo-path canonicalization),
121	/// while `vc-x1 push`'s `squash-push-bot` stage constructs it
122	/// directly.
123	#[derive(Debug)]
124	pub struct SquashPushParams {
125	    pub repo: PathBuf,
126	    pub squash: SquashSpec,
127	    pub bookmark: String,
128	    /// This run is the user's at-rest invocation rather than
129	    /// `vc-x1 push`'s `squash-push-bot` stage.
130	    ///
131	    /// Everything addressed to a person is gated on it: the
132	    /// publish-mismatch report, the precheck's and after-check's
133	    /// lines, and the prompt. Mid-push every one of them is wrong.
134	    /// The mismatch is the normal state there, since `bookmark-set`
135	    /// just moved the bookmark and this stage is what publishes it.
136	    /// The verdict lines describe a repo caught mid-sequence. And
137	    /// nobody is watching to answer a prompt.
138	    ///
139	    /// What is not gated is the precheck's decision. A stage with
140	    /// nothing to do should still do nothing, which is the behavior
141	    /// the `already sync'd` early return gave push before the
142	    /// precheck replaced it.
143	    pub at_rest: bool,
144	    /// Act without asking once the precheck has found work. True is
145	    /// today's behavior and the built-in default, so the prompt is
146	    /// opt-in. Resolved from `--yes`, then `--ask`, then the repo's
147	    /// `squash-push.yes`, then the built-in.
148	    pub yes: bool,
149	    /// Print what the precheck found and the steps it would take,
150	    /// and change nothing.
151	    pub dry_run: bool,
152	    /// Allow a forced push, which is refused without it.
153	    pub force: bool,
154	}
155	
156	/// The `yes` choice: the flags, then the config key, then the
157	/// built-in default.
158	///
159	/// The same order `agent-files diff` resolves its `--custom` by. A
160	/// boolean flag cannot turn a configured `true` back off, which is
161	/// why `--ask` exists rather than a `--no-yes`.
162	pub fn resolve_yes(yes: bool, ask: bool, key_value: Option<bool>, default: bool) -> bool {
163	    if yes {
164	        true
165	    } else if ask {
166	        false
167	    } else {
168	        key_value.unwrap_or(default)
169	    }
170	}

172	/// The `squash-push.yes` key of the config in `repo`, if any.
173	///
174	/// Read from the repo the command is pointed at rather than from the
175	/// workspace, so each side may answer differently and a plain repo
176	/// outside a workspace simply has no answer.
177	fn config_yes(repo: &Path) -> Result<Option<bool>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
178	    let Some(cfg) = crate::config_md::load(repo)? else {
179	        return Ok(None);
180	    };
181	    match crate::toml_simple::toml_get(&cfg.map, "squash-push.yes").map(String::as_str) {
182	        None => Ok(None),
183	        Some("true") => Ok(Some(true)),
184	        Some("false") => Ok(Some(false)),
185	        Some(other) => Err(format!(
186	            "squash-push.yes: invalid bool {other:?}: expected true or false, unquoted"
187	        )
188	        .into()),
189	    }
190	}

192	/// The params for one resolved repo: the `--squash` default filled
193	/// and `--bookmark` mapped straight over, or read from the repo when
194	/// absent. `repo` is already canonical, the resolver's.
195	fn params_for(a: &SquashPushArgs, repo: PathBuf) -> Result<SquashPushParams, String> {
196	    {
197	        let yes = resolve_yes(
198	            a.yes,
199	            a.ask,
200	            config_yes(&repo).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?,
201	            crate::config_schema::SQUASH_PUSH_YES_DEFAULT,
202	        );
203	        let squash = a.squash.value.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| SquashSpec {
204	            source: "@".to_string(),

206	        }); // OK: --squash absent -> the command's default @,@- pair
207	        let bookmark = match &a.bookmark {
208	            Some(b) => b.clone(),
209	            None => current_bookmark(&repo, &squash.target).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?,
210	        };
211	        Ok(SquashPushParams {
212	            repo,
213	            squash: squash.clone(),
214	            bookmark,
215	            at_rest: true,
216	            yes,
217	            dry_run: a.dry_run.value,
218	            force: a.force,

content.content:
a coordinated force-push of history someone else may already hold. Approval is the one moment the
user can still say no at no cost.

#### At rest

The agent-repo is a live journal, so everything after a publishing command, its own record included,
lands after it, and the agent cannot bring its own `@` to a fixed point. So the session's tail is
folded by the user after the session, the one moment the journal is still, by a squash-push into
the last agent commit, which keeps the change id the `ochid:`s name (wink, 2026-11-09). An archive
wants both repos clean. A squash-push into a published commit would rewrite a trunk others may
hold, so it is refused, and after a Land the agent published the tail rides the next opening.

Either order is correct (wink, 2026-11-09). The agent-repo went first while `ocid:` pinned the
agent commit's SHA, so the work commit naming it was pushed only once that SHA was final. With
`orepo:` and `ochid:` each side names the other by change id, which neither push changes, so one
`squash-push -s b` publishes both.

content.content:
### squash-push

Squash `@` into `@-`, advance a bookmark, and push, capturing a repo's trailing working-copy writes
and publish them in one step. Folding into a commit already on the remote would rewrite published
history and force the push, so it is refused unless `--force` allows it, and a fold into an unpublished
commit pushes as a fast-forward.

The primary use case is folding the bot repo's session tail: session data keeps landing in `@` after

# Say what it found and what it would do, and change nothing
vc-x1 squash-push -s a --dry-run

# Amend a work-in-progress bookmark's published commit on purpose, a forced push
vc-x1 squash-push -s w --bookmark feature --force
```

`-s` is required and `-R` optional, as for every write command: `-s` says which repos, `-R` says
|------|-------------|
| `--bookmark <NAME>` | Bookmark to advance and push [default: the line's own, see above]; the old positional is refused, naming this flag |
| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Path to jj repo [default: .] |
| `--squash [<SOURCE,TARGET>]` | Squash pair [default: @,@-] |
| `-y, --yes` | Act without asking, once the precheck found work |
| `--ask` | Ask before acting, overriding a configured `squash-push.yes` |
| `--force` | Allow a forced push, for a work-in-progress bookmark's deliberate amend, never a trunk |

Behavior notes:

- Runs synchronously, so a failure is a visible non-zero exit. (Replaces the `finalize`
  addressed to a person, and mid-push there is neither a person to read them nor a settled state
  worth describing: the mismatch is normal there, since push's `bookmark-set` just moved the
  bookmark and this stage is what publishes it. The precheck's decision still applies, so a stage
  with nothing to do still does nothing.
- It refuses a forced push before changing anything. When the squash would fold into a target already
  in `::<bookmark>@origin`, or `<bookmark>@origin` is not an ancestor of the target, the push would be
  forced, so it errors with "squash-push: the push of '<bm>' would be forced, since <why>, so nothing
  is changed. The tail rides the next commit, or --force rewrites it anyway". A bookmark with no
  remote yet is never refused by this check.
- Preflight refuses bad states before rewriting anything: unresolvable squash revsets, an
  ochid-dropping squash (see [Testing the ochid-trailer guard](#testing-the-ochid-trailer-guard)),
  conflicts, a missing / untracked / non-forward bookmark, an undescribed push target.

precondition and does nothing when its work is already done, so re-running after a failure is simply
running. If a run fails, push stops and reports. A half that fails before its own push restores the
repo it touched via `jj op restore` to a snapshot taken moments earlier in the same process. Once a
half's push succeeds that half is published: from there a change is either a new pair on top, or an
amend of what was pushed, where [`squash-push`](#squash-push) refuses the forced update unless
`--force` allows it. See the protocol's
[at-rest contract](AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push).

| Flag | Description |
echo hello > "$work/hello.txt"
jj describe @ -R "$work" -m 'feat: add hello.txt'
jj bookmark set main -r @ -R "$work"
jj git push -R "$work"

# 2. bot repo: trailing writes -> squash-push (fold into @-, push)
echo notes > "$bot/notes.md"
vc-x1 squash-push -s a -R "$bot" --force

# 3. cleanup when done (init also created a symlink under
#    ~/.claude/projects/ pointing at the fixture, remove it too)
rm -rf "$parent"
```

**Why `jj git push` for the work repo but `squash-push` for `.claude`?** The work repo's workflow is
a plain dev commit on `@-` that we push directly. The bot repo mirrors the bot's runtime pattern:
session writes land in `@` (above the last committed commit), and squash-push folds those trailing
writes into that commit just before pushing, so one atomic state goes upstream.

The fixture's bot `main` is already pushed, so folding into it is a forced push and the example
passes `--force`. The run is synchronous, no background child, so what you see is the whole flow:
```
$ vc-x1 squash-push -s a -R "$bot" --force
squash-push: squashing @ -> @-...
squash-push: setting bookmark 'main' to @-...
squash-push: pushing 'main' to origin...
squash-push: done
```

Preflight failures (bookmark missing, non-tracking remote, squash revset unresolved, conflicts, push
target lacks a description) exit with a non-zero status and a pointed error on stderr before
anything is rewritten.

### Testing the ochid-trailer guard

`squash-push` refuses to drop `ochid:` trailers: when the squash source's message carries trailers
the destination's message lacks, `--use-destination-message` would silently discard them and leave
the counterpart repo's cross-links dangling (the incident is recorded in [record finalize ochid-loss
bug (0.65.1)](./notes/chores/chores-13.md#docs-record-finalize-ochid-loss-bug-0651)). The guard runs
in preflight, before anything is rewritten.

throwaway init fixture (same shape as [Testing push + squash-push](#testing-push--squash-push))
using its bot repo:

content.content:
A work commit named its agent partner by SHA in `ocid:` and the
partner's parents by SHA in `pcid:`, so a squash-push of the agent-repo,
a rebase, or a describe made them stale, and neither repo could be left
clean after a session. The rules also named a squash-push that cannot
run and published the agent-repo first, an order only `ocid:` needed.

Solution: both sides stamp `orepo:`, the other repo's URL, above their
`ochid:` change ids, and a restamp gives older `ocid:` and `pcid:` way
to it, so no trailer holds a SHA. The journal folds into any unpublished
partner, `squash-push -s b` is the clean-up after a session and asks before
a forced push, and push, land, and squash-push all publish the shared
work-repo first. Acquaint reports the vc-x1 builds, and a rung's dev
build is installed before its review. See details in TODO.md.

Rung -2 now has the change. A forced push asks first, and the `--yes` flag on the command line is the only advance answer. Full validation passed (864 tests), and the dr-1 fixture builder ran clean with the new build.

**What `squash-push` does now:**
- **The warning:** when a push would be forced, it says why: "the push of 'main' is forced, since …".
- **The question:** it asks "rewrite the published 'main@origin'? [y/N]".
- **`--yes`:** passing it on the command line answers yes ahead of time. A configured `squash-push.yes` does not.
- **No terminal:** without a terminal and without `--yes`, it changes nothing and says "--yes rewrites it, or run it at a terminal to be asked".
- **Inside `push` and `land`:** squash-push never forces there, since nobody is there to ask.
- **`--force` is gone.**

**Also changed:**
- **The test** is now `a_forced_push_asks_and_yes_answers`. It checks the run without a terminal, the run inside `push`, and the `--yes` run.
- **The dr-1 fixture builder:** `build-dr-1.py` uses `--yes`. The tests use a prebuilt copy of the fixture, so I rebuilt it in a scratch directory with the new dev build to check.
- **AGENTS.md, At rest:** squash-push asks, `--yes` answers, and I pass it only for a forced push you approved.
- **rationale.md:** a new entry, "A forced push asks rather than refuses", with your reasons: topic bookmarks have few readers, a mistake after a push needs an amend, and agent repos are personal but public.
- **README, the `--help` text and TODO.md** match.

**Rung -2 itself.** The fold was done with `vc-x1 squash`, and its description changed "refuses a forced push" to "asks before a forced push". `pmtvruwwsrvo` is now `421f14bd0cdb`, and its trailers are unchanged. validate-desc still passes on both rungs, and `vc-x1-dev` is reinstalled from the committed tree.

The push is ready on your approval:

```
vc-x1-dev push -s b
```

It pushes the cycle bookmark up to -2, then folds the journal into `msxzosrsqltq` and pushes agent `main`.

The plain version: squash-push no longer refuses a rewrite of something already pushed. It asks, and `--yes` typed on the command line is the advance answer. The change is in rung -2, which is ready to push when you say so.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Agent, AskUserQuestion, Bash, Edit, Read, SubagentHandback, Write</tools-used-before-summary>
</system-reminder>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **The cycle.** "chore: complete vc-x1, ready for vc-x2" is on bookmark `chore-complete-vc-x1-ready-for-vc-x2`. The ladder, in `zTOC.md`:
     - 0 (done) the opening, pushed.
     - 1 (done) "feat: trailers --update rewrites a whole history", `tlsszorkmswv`.
     - 2 (done) "feat: orepo replaces ocid and pcid", `pmtvruwwsrvo`.
     - "chore: a test vc-x2 reaches vc-x1's history".
     - The closing.
   - **Version.** 0.85.21-2, agent-files v0.3.1-3.
   - **The user's decisions this stretch:**
     - Incorporate all changes from the test workspace `~/tmp/wt-21-3-1`, and fix the "likely lost" warning.
     - Fix the validate-agent wording.
     - Make `land --push`/`push` publish in the same order as `squash-push -s b`, work first.
     - State that the work-repo goes first because it is shared, so its push is the one likely refused.
     - Commit the orepo rung.
     - Restamp -1 and make one agent commit covering -1 and -2.
     - Pushing both repos is good (the push itself has not been run).
     - 1:1 work/agent pairs going forward. I proposed a new rung "feat: a rung commits as a pair" before the vc-x2 test rung.
     - Agent repos are "personal but public", observed and not cloned, to be explored more in vc-x2.
     - A forced push should be allowed with `--yes` (a confirmation, not a refusal), on both sides. "go, fold it into -2".
   - **Messages rename (thoughts only so far).** Move `vc-x1-messages` to maybe `~/vc-family-messages`. I suggested a separate rung before the vc-x2 test rung, and the GitHub repo rename is the user's.
   - **Protocol rules:**
     - Every push needs the user's explicit approval. "please review" goes as its own message.
     - When piping cargo or vc-x1, use `set -o pipefail`. Never echo `$?`.
     - Lines wrap at 100 characters. No semicolons in prose. Speculation is marked "We think".
     - End a technical explanation with "The plain version:".
     - The agent passes `--yes` for a forced push only with the user's approval.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Trailers.** `orepo:` (the other repo's URL) above `ochid:` change ids, both sides. No trailer holds a SHA. Old `ocid:`/`pcid:` go on a restamp.
   - **Push order.** Either order is correct, and work first is preferred because the work-repo is the shared one.
   - **`push -s b` sequence:**
     - agent local steps (commit the journal as partner if Pending/Changed);
     - work half (restamp if needed, set the bookmark, push);
     - agent publish (`AgentPublish::Main` uses `publish_agent_main`, `AgentPublish::SquashPush` folds and pushes).
   - **`land --push`** goes through push.
   - **Forced push in squash-push:**
     - It warns, then prompts on a tty.
     - Only the explicit `--yes` flag (`forced_yes`) answers. A configured `squash-push.yes` does not.
     - With no tty and no `--yes` it is an error that changes nothing.
     - Push's stage (`at_rest` false) never forces.
   - **Agent repo `@`** is the session's live data, so it is dirty mid-session. A tail after a push rides the next commit.
   - **Mid-cycle backup.** `commit -s a --covers <revset>` makes an N:1 agent commit.
   - **validate-desc quirk.** `-r` with a `::` range checks only one commit. Use `-r <tip> -n N`.
   - **The dr-1 fixture** is prebuilt in `../vc-x1-fixtures`, so the tests don't rebuild it. To rebuild: `VC_X1=vc-x1-dev python3 support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py <dir> --local`.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **AGENTS.md** (copied from the test workspace, then edited):
     - Acquaint step 3, Tools: `vc-x1 -V` and `vc-x1-dev -V`. The steps after it are renumbered.
     - At rest item 2 now reads: "`vc-x1 squash-push -s b` pushes the work trunk first, the shared repo and so the push likely to be refused, then folds the tail into the Land's agent commit and pushes it, so each `main` moves once, forward. `squash-push` asks before a push that would be forced, a published commit rewritten, and the `--yes` flag answers, so the agent passes it only for a forced push the user approved."
   - **agent-data/jj.md**: Land step 3: "`vc-x1 push -s b --bookmark <trunk>`, the work repo first, the journal folded into the Land's agent commit while that is unpublished… by `vc-x1 squash-push -s b`".
   - **agent-data/rationale.md**:
     - The tools-check paragraph, and a "### Tools the session runs" section (both from the test).
     - At rest paragraph: "After a Land the agent published, the tail rides the next opening."
     - New paragraph "A forced push asks rather than refuses (wink, 2026-11-09)…": topic bookmarks have few readers, a mistake after a push wants an amend, only the `--yes` flag answers, and the agent-repo is personal but public.
     - "Either order is correct (wink, 2026-11-09)…" and "Work first is preferred (wink, 2026-11-09)…".
   - **agent-data/versioning.md**: the merged bullet "**Which build runs**: for this project's artifact or another project's tool the session runs, `vc-x1` the common one, acquaint reports `<tool> -V` and `<tool>-dev -V`… ([why](rationale.md#tools-the-session-runs))".
   - **src/squash_push.rs**:
     - Args: `force` removed. The `yes` doc now says "a forced push included".
     - Params: `pub forced_yes: bool`, documented as "The `--yes` flag itself, never the config key". `params_for` sets `forced_yes: a.yes`.
     - preflight:
       ```rust
       if !params.at_rest && !params.forced_yes && let Some(why) = forced_push(repo, sq, bookmark)? {
           return Err(format!("squash-push: the push of '{bookmark}' would be forced, since {why}, so nothing is changed").into());
       }
       ```
     - squash_push:
       - `let forced = if params.at_rest { forced_push(...)? } else { None };`
       - If forced: `warn!("squash-push: the push of '{bookmark}' is forced, since {why}")`. Otherwise the publish-state info lines, with Mismatch reading "'{bm}' is at {local} here and {remote} on origin, below the squash target: this run will publish it".
       - The dry run has the line "would force-push … asking first unless --yes".
       - Then `match &forced { Some(why) => confirm_forced(params, why, ctx.stdin_is_tty)?, None => confirm(...)? }`.
     - New fn `confirm_forced`:
       - `forced_yes` passes.
       - Non-tty errors with "…would be forced, since {why}, so nothing is changed: --yes rewrites it, or run it at a terminal to be asked".
       - Otherwise it prompts "rewrite the published '{bm}@origin'? [y/N]", and a decline is an error.
     - Module and struct docs updated.
     - Tests: `force:` became `forced_yes:`. The test `a_forced_push_asks_and_yes_answers` checks the refusal without a tty (even with config yes), refusal with `at_rest=false`, then `forced_yes=true` succeeds.
   - **src/push.rs**:
     - `enum AgentPublish { Main, SquashPush }`.
     - `agent_half` returns `(String, AgentPublish)` with no pushes. The new `fn agent_publish(ctx, pair, how)`.
     - `push_in` runs the agent local steps, then the work half, then agent publish, with step gates.
     - The comment states either order is correct and work first is preferred.
     - The module doc is rewritten. `forced_yes: false`.
   - **src/push/integration_tests.rs**: the new test `push_publishes_the_work_repo_first`. It breaks the work remote URL, checks the agent partner is committed locally and agent `main@origin` hasn't moved, restores the URL, and confirms a rerun publishes both.
   - **src/land.rs**:
     - Docs say `--push` publishes "the work repo first".
     - `forced_yes: false`.
     - Its non-at_work_head path already pushed work then agent.
   - **src/main.rs**:
     - push long help: three steps, the work-first order.
     - land help: "the work repo first".
     - squash-push help: asks before a forced push, `--yes` answers.
   - **src/common.rs**:
     - `verify_bot_published` Mismatch now reads "'{bm}' is at {} here and {} on origin, so it is not published: publish it with `vc-x1 squash-push -s a -R {repo}`, then retry".
     - The `bookmark_publish_state` doc is updated.
   - **src/validate_bot.rs**: the test asserts `"is not published"`.
   - **support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py**: `--force` removed, `--yes` kept, at two sites.
   - **README.md**:
     - land "the work repo first".
     - push table: three rows (agent local, work, agent publish).
     - squash-push section: asks, `--yes` answers. Examples use `--yes`, the flags table drops `--force`, the behavior notes are rewritten, and the testing sections say `--yes`.
   - **TODO.md**:
     - The deliberation "Clean by squash-push" now says `squash-push -s b`, work first, and asks with `--yes`.
     - Orepo rung subsection bullets: the test workspace's two gaps; the squash-push warning fix and the validate-agent wording; push, land and squash-push all work first; asks before a forced push, `--yes` flag only.
   - **zTOC.md**: rung 2 is `(done)`.
   - **tmp/orepo-body.txt**: rung -2's commit body. The final version says "`squash-push -s b` is the clean-up after a session and asks before a forced push, and push, land, and squash-push all publish the shared work-repo first."
   - **custom.md**: now says v0.3.1-3. It is untracked.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **`agent-files copy` refuses a working copy that already changes the set.** Copied the four files with `cp`, then `agent-files diff` showed 0 of 15 differ.
   - **The bash-guard hook denied piped vc-x1/cargo commands.** Added `set -o pipefail`.
   - **`validate-desc -s b -r 'tlsszorkmswv::…'`** failed in the agent repo with "Revision doesn't exist". Ran each side separately, and used `-r pmtvruwwsrvo -n 2` because the `::` range checked only one commit.
   - **Compile error** "struct SquashPushArgs has no field named forced_yes" from the blanket replace. Removed that line from the Args literal in the test.
   - **Wrong claim corrected:** I first said README:2141 needed changing, then found `land --push` did push agent first. The user later asked to change the code, so it was done.
   - **User correction:** "I've done `vc-x1{-dev} squash-push -s a` many times… why would it be refused now?" and "I thought I'd gated that with the land." This led to the `--yes` confirmation design.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Validation.** Full validation passes, 864 tests plus the integration tests. The dr-1 fixture rebuilds with the dev build in the scratchpad at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-wink-data-prgs-rust-vc-x1/9dc021c3-9cec-4bbb-a7c2-502f1021001f/scratchpad/dr1`.

   - **Installed.** `vc-x1-dev` is 0.85.21-2+421f14bd0cdb, clean, from the committed tree. Plain vc-x1 is 0.85.20.
